editorial.headline: Ceramic Household Ware with a Real Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers clay and ceramic household, decorative, technical and packaging goods, with national PMA openness and no Bali moratorium block in the record.
editorial.body:
This activity is the manufacturing home of everyday clay and ceramic objects: plates, cups, bowls, pitchers, teapots, cooking pots, jars and similar household ware. Its scope also reaches display and decorative pieces such as statues, flower vases, betel containers, cigarette boxes and piggy banks. The record is not limited to ornamental craft; it also includes technical ceramic products such as insulators, insulating fittings and permanent magnets, as well as jars and similar products used to transport or package goods.

That breadth matters because it describes a production activity rather than a retail label or a purely artistic category. A founder registering under this code is placing the business in the making of clay or ceramic goods for use, display, technical application, transport or packaging. The same activity can therefore sit behind a small workshop producing tableware, a decorative ceramics operation, or a larger facility making more functional ceramic components, provided the activity remains within the stated manufacturing scope.

The scale position is unusually straightforward in the slim record: it is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In practical editorial terms, that means the code is not reserved in the record for only one size of operator. It can describe a micro producer, a small or medium manufacturer, or a large-scale industrial setup. The record gives no extra thresholds, capital figures, local licences, tax treatment or timing requirements, so none should be read into it. Its core message is scope and access: clay and ceramic household, decorative, technical and packaging goods, open across all listed business scales.

The national foreign-investment picture is also clear. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does not add a block in this record. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the reason is specific: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk level is medium-high/high, so Bali's island-wide moratorium on low and medium-low-risk PMA registrations does not block it. The honest conclusion is therefore not a hidden restriction but a clean distinction: nationally, the code is fully foreign-open in the record, and in Bali it is not blocked by the stated moratorium.
